title: Neurophysiology / Electrodiagnostic Test Catalog
note: Tests run by Clinical Neurophysiologist / Neurologist. Each with purpose, role, EEG-linkage (when it depends-on or complements EEG), and status. §155 honest.

tests.name: NCV (Nerve Conduction Velocity)
tests.eeg_link: independent — pairs with EEG for systemic/peripheral involvement
tests.case_data: MRS.VEENA CHANDRA NCV.pdf, MR RAMKESH NCV-EMG.pdf

tests.name: EMG (Electromyography)
tests.eeg_link: complements EEG in epilepsy with motor signs / myoclonus

tests.name: SSEP (Somatosensory Evoked Potentials)
tests.eeg_link: evoked-potential — giant SSEP linked to cortical myoclonus/epilepsy

tests.name: Autonomic Function Tests
tests.eeg_link: SUDEP risk — autonomic dysfunction is a key EEG-epilepsy comorbidity

tests.name: RR Variation (HRV)
tests.eeg_link: STRONG — peri-ictal HR change + SUDEP risk; pairs with EEG seizure timing

eeg_linkage_summary.link: Evoked potentials — same electrophysiology family as EEG; assess specific pathways EEG can't isolate
Autonomic — SUDEP risk; peri-ictal cardiac/autonomic change time-locked to EEG seizures
Motor — distinguishes epileptic myoclonus (cortical, EEG-correlated) from non-epileptic
Peripheral — independent of EEG; rules out systemic/peripheral mimics

summary.honest_note: EEG built; VEEG/RR/autonomic partial. NCV/EMG/BERA/VEP/BLINK/SSEP/RNS/ABPM/SSR cataloged — Case 1 already has real NCV/EMG/BERA/VEP report PDFs (extractable via RAG). EEG-linkage column shows which tests depend-on/complement EEG (evoked potentials + autonomic = strongest linkage for epilepsy/SUDEP).
